title: Late Breaking Results: A real-time diffusion-based filter for human pose estimation on edge devices
problem: CNN-based human pose estimation systems exhibit inherent inaccuracy, and existing filtering models that refine inference results are computationally intensive, preventing deployment on resource-constrained edge devices.
motivation: Human pose estimation is increasingly critical in healthcare and Industry 5.0 applications, demanding real-time performance with minimal computational overhead on edge devices.
method: The approach uses a diffusion model—a neural network trained to gradually remove noise—to clean up inaccurate pose predictions. To work efficiently on phones and embedded devices with limited power, the researchers test different noise levels to find the best settings. They then validate the approach on readily available edge hardware using both artificially generated noise and real-world errors from existing pose estimation systems.
key_novelty: Using diffusion models to filter human pose estimation errors on phones and embedded devices, efficiently enough for real-time video.
contributions: Real-time diffusion-based filtering technique optimized for edge devices
Micro-benchmarking framework for analyzing noise response and selecting optimal configurations
Demonstration of significant performance improvement with minimal computational overhead
Evaluation methodology combining synthetic and real noise from HPE systems

metrics.accuracy: significant improvement reported but quantitative metrics not provided

limitations: Preliminary results stage; specific quantitative metrics for speedup and accuracy improvements not detailed in abstract.
primary_theme: Efficient edge filtering for pose estimation using diffusion models
